postmerge_editorial_corrections.from: Three critical items are not met (4: English-only published articles without justification; 11: incompatible pooled risk ratios and inconsistent model description; 13: risk of bias never discussed), which gives critically low confidence under the AMSTAR 2 rules whatever item 7 turns out to be. This is a judgment about the pooled numbers, not about the raw counts, which are transparent: Table 1 lets a reader see that about half of the people with panic disorder and almost no controls had a panic attack after caffeine, and that none was reported after placebo. Citable for: those proportions, the doses and conditions studied (selected oral protocols, mostly 480 mg as printed, at rest, off medication; the caffeine-citrate basis is unresolved). Not citable for: a precise risk ratio, a placebo-controlled size of the anxiety effect, effects of everyday caffeine intake, or mechanisms.
